problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=5{x}^{2}y-4x+2{y}^{3}-6{y}^{2}.
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,1]^{T}.$

| $[$ | {{field-1}} | $10$ | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | $-6$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $10$ | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(5{x}^{2}y-4x+2{y}^{3}-6{y}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(5{x}^{2}y-4x+2{y}^{3}-6{y}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10xy-4 \\ 5{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2}-12y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(10xy-4) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(5{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2}-12y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(10xy-4) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(5{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2}-12y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10y & 10x \\ 10x & 12y-12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}10y & 10x \\ 10x & 12y-12\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}10xy-4 \\ 5{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2}-12y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}10y & 10x \\ 10x & 12y-12\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}10xy-4 \\ 5{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2}-12y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}10(1) & 10(1) \\ 10(1) & 12(1)-12\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}10(1)(1)-4 \\ 5(1)^{2}+6(1)^{2}-12(1)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}10 & 10 \\ 10 & 0\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
